finding.statement: The donor already proves exact VectorControl packet delivery and separately proves deterministic construction of a native llama.cpp cvec buffer. The reviewed causal closure does not yet demonstrate that the exact native cvec binding (including scale, layer range and buffer digest) was the intervention actually active for the exact model invocation named by ModelExecution/InferenceReceipt/J-Space. Therefore packet delivery must not be promoted into hidden-state cvec intervention causality.
not_claimed: no claim that current runtime applies the wrong vector
no claim that cvec application is absent from all unreviewed source

hypothesis: A producer/executor-owned preinvocation observation that binds exact LlamaCppCVecBinding identity plus applied context/invocation identity before decode, and is then carried into ModelExecution/InferenceReceipt/J-Space, will close the native hidden-state intervention identity edge needed for model-specific J-Space causal experiments.
counterhypotheses: An existing executor or preinvocation primitive outside the reviewed files may already bind the native cvec state; if so, this is a discovery/indexing gap rather than an architecture gap.

Binding a source-generated cvec receipt alone would still be insufficient: the runtime may fail to apply it, apply another vector, clear it, or mutate layer/scale state before decode. The useful evidence must be executor/runtime observed rather than caller-declared.
Even exact cvec application identity does not prove behavioral causality; paired baseline/control/intervention runs plus target and off-target measurements remain required.
cheapest_high_information_discriminator: On an exposed authorized zero-cost local or clay-direct-dev runtime, instrument the exact llama.cpp pre-decode cvec application boundary to emit an executor-owned observation binding invocation_id/context identity, checkpoint/runtime identity, LlamaCppCVecBinding.binding_sha256, cvec_f32le_sha256, il_start, il_end and strength. Run paired no-cvec vs cvec application at fixed prompt/seed/model identity and verify the observation reaches ModelExecution/J-Space without caller-supplied aliases. Do not implement a new canonical guard until this runtime observation either confirms a missing edge or identifies an existing one.
